title: Lobster Thermidor
subtitle: French grilled lobster with cream and mustard sauce
excerpt: Halved cooked lobster returned to its shell with a sauce of shallots, dry vermouth, cream, mustard, and tarragon, grilled under a hot grill until the sauce is bubbling and golden. The great French restaurant lobster dish, made at home.

recipe.sourceNotes: Lobster Thermidor was created in Paris in 1894 at Chez Marie restaurant to celebrate the premiere of a play called Thermidor (named after the month in the French revolutionary calendar corresponding to July to August). The dish was brought to wider attention through Escoffier's kitchen at the Savoy Hotel in London. It is named after the play, which is named after the calendar month, which comes from the Greek word for heat (therme). The dish is defined by its sauce: a reduction of shallots and white wine or vermouth finished with cream, Dijon mustard, and tarragon or chervil. The prepared lobster is put back in its shell with the sauce and grilled to finish.

content.text: Use a cooked lobster; ask the fishmonger to cook it for you if you prefer. The sauce should be quite thick before going back into the shell so it does not run out under the grill. The grill must be at maximum heat so the sauce bubbles and browns in 3 to 4 minutes without drying out the lobster meat.

items.preparation: approximately 700 g; cooked; halved lengthways, meat removed from shell and claws

content.text: Remove the lobster meat from the halved shells and claws. Reserve the shells. Cut the tail meat into 2 cm pieces. Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Cook the shallots for 3 minutes until soft. Add the wine and reduce by half. Add the cream and reduce by a third. Stir in the mustard, dill or tarragon, lemon juice, and cayenne. Season.

Heat the grill to maximum. Add the lobster meat to the sauce and warm through briefly over low heat, 1 to 2 minutes. Spoon the lobster and sauce back into the reserved shells. Scatter with grated parmesan.
Grill for 3 to 4 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and the parmesan is golden. Serve immediately with crusty bread.
